superi: superus, -a, -um — above, upper; superī (m. pl.), the gods above (gen. sg. m.; nom. pl. m.)
surgentia: surgō, -ere, surrēxī — to rise, arise, grow (pres. part., n. nom./acc. pl.)
tacitum: tacitus, -a, -um — silent, unspoken, secret (n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)
tanta: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. abl. sg. (ex tantā urbe)
tantum: tantus, -a, -um — so great; tantum (n. acc. sg.), so great a thing; (adv.) only, so much · also m. acc. sg. (tantum dolorem)
tela: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (acc./nom. pl.)
templa: templum, -ī (n.) — temple, sanctuary, sacred precinct (acc./nom. pl.)
terra: terra, -ae (f.) — land, earth, ground (nom./abl. sg.) · also f. voc. sg. (ō terra hospita)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
tota: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
tristi: tristis, -e — sad, grim, bitter, harsh (m./f./n. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
troiae: Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (gen. sg.) · also dat. sg., for Troy (sīc fāta ferēbant)
tulisset: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — to carry, bring, bear (3rd sg. plupf. subj.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tumulum: tumulus, -ī (m.) — mound, hillock, burial mound (acc. sg.)
tuorum: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.); tuōrum, of your people (m. gen. pl.)
ultra: ultrā (adv.) — beyond, further, more · also prep. + acc., beyond (vīrēs ultrā, beyond strength)
umbra: umbra, -ae (f.) — shade, shadow (abl. sg.; nom. sg.)
una: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (f. abl./nom. sg.); ūnā (adv.), together · also ūnā, adv., once (satis ūnā superque, enough once and more)
unaque: ūnā (adv.) — together, at the same time, in one company + -que, and
unus: ūnus, -a, -um — one, alone, a single (m. nom. sg.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
vagantur: vagor, -ārī, -ātus sum — to wander, range about, ride at large (dep.) (3rd pl. pres.)
vel: vel (conj., adv.) — or; even; vel… vel, either… or
veris: vērus, -a, -um — true; vēra (n. pl.) the truth (n. abl. pl.; also m. dat./abl. pl.)
vero: vērō (adv.) — in truth, indeed, but; tum vērō, then indeed
vertice: vertex, verticis (m.) — peak, summit; whirl (abl. sg.)
videbat: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd sg. impf.)
videbis: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (2nd sg. fut.)
videre: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (pres. inf.)
vires: vīs (f.) — force; pl. vīrēs, strength (acc. pl.) · also nom. pl. (fractae vīrēs)
virum: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero (acc. sg.; also gen. pl., old form = virōrum)
vis: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, power, violence; pl. vīrēs, strength (nom. sg.)
visa: videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
viscera: viscus, vīsceris (n.) — flesh; pl. viscera, entrails (acc. pl.)
vobis: tū, tuī — you; vōs, vōbīs, to/for you, by you (dat./abl. pl.)
voltus: vultus (voltus), -ūs (m.) — face, look, expression (nom. sg.; acc. pl.) · also nom. pl. (haerent … voltus)
